newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures mostly end down in correction.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures mostly end down in correction.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended down slightly Monday in moderate trade, pressured by technical selling after last week's late rally despite firmer cash and news of some U.S. Gulf production cuts.
November slipped 2.7 cents to close at $2.369 per million British thermal units. December settled unchanged at $2.556. Most other deferreds ended steady to down two cents.

"I think we'll see more sideways action ahead but I don't see us going a whole bunch lower because of the time of year," said one New York-based futures trader, adding technicals looked more constructive after last week's move up.

Traders said U.S. Gulf natgas production cuts as a precaution against Tropical Storm Josephine probably totaled about 2 bcfd, including 650 mmcfd on Transco, 350 mmcfd on Texas Eastern, 350 mmcfd on Trunkline and 150 mmcfd on ANR.
But they noted no platform damage had been reported and most agreed the reductions would be temporary and have little market impact.

At 1400 EDT, Tropical Storm Josephine, with winds of 70 mph, was 110 miles south-southwest of Apalachicola, Florida, and moving northeast at 23 mph. Forecasters said it was likely to become a hurricane before landfall sometime Monday night.
Technically, support in November was seen at just under $2.30 and then in the $2.16-2.175 area. Resistance was pegged in the $2.41-2.43 range.
Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices firmed five to 10 cents Monday to the $2.15-2.20 level. Midcon prices were pegged more than five cents higher in the mid-$1.90s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell one-half cent to $2.215. NYMEX said 36,992 Hub contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 45,152.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled up one cent at $1.045, while deferreds closed mixed. NYMEX said 108 Alberta contracts traded.
NYMEX November Permian natgas was untraded but closed unchanged at $2.01, while deferreds were mixed. NYMEX said 100 Permian lots changed hands versus 50 on Friday.

On the KCBT, November settled one cent lower at $2.09, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.7 cents to 27.9 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 93 lots traded, down from Friday's 133.
